feature: Refresh pallet balance and retire confirmed deleted or cancelled reservations

setup.dependencies: Existing test image and Node/fast-check/c8/TypeScript/ESLint only; no new dependencies.
setup.git: Preserve workspace edits; no commits or resets.
setup.tests: Standard bounded isolated Compose; teardown registered before startup.
setup.deployment: Carry the correction through the existing authorized feature rollout, preserve gate values, use app-only image overlay and rollback. NetSuite writes prohibited in diagnostics.

scenarios: F1 Every customer or Sales Order pallet enquiry reads fresh NetSuite activity; submission rechecks the latest balance.

D1 A previously verified direct CM absent from fresh activity is read by its exact internal ID. Only HTTP 404 with NONEXISTENT_ID confirms deletion. Mark the linked batch and records cancelled/Deleted, preserve intent and remote identity, and audit the finding.
D2 A deleted CM is never recreated by retry, repeated lookup, concurrent lookup, or background reconciliation.
S1 Permission failures, generic 404s, malformed success bodies and transport errors do not confirm deletion, do not release reservations, and fail the enquiry.
S2 Pending, unverified, local-only and uncertain creation records remain reserved; a CM still present but not yet indexed stays reserved.
C1 Confirmed cancelled/voided transactions release pallet and stock reservations; live RA reservations remain intact. Combined CM deletion releases both components.
R1 Existing return/gate tests remain green; API privacy, yard restrictions, idempotency and proof requirements remain unchanged.
E1 The sample customer balance refresh reconciles through ordinary application code without editing business records manually or creating any NetSuite transaction.

failureModel.falseDeletion: Strict NetSuite error code tests plus generated error cases; never infer deletion solely from SuiteQL absence.
failureModel.duplicateCredit: Identity preservation, concurrent lookup/retry tests and mutation.
failureModel.overReturn: Unverified and local-only reservations; before-submit fresh balance and existing concurrency regression.
failureModel.staleBalance: Immediate consecutive customer/order enquiries after remote changes, cache regression test.
failureModel.partialLocalState: Atomic durable cancelled state for batch/records with audit; existing intent preserved.
failureModel.hostImpact: mbbs-tests.slice standard resource budgets, cleanup logs, production health checks.

knownLimits: NetSuite cannot provide a transaction spanning its balance read and a later Operator action; the app rechecks before admission and retains local concurrency protection.
Error handling uses Oracle documented NONEXISTENT_ID; no financial transactions will be created in live verification.
